# Churchill Downs Stakes Advances: Consequent Bids to Stay Unbeaten in Thanksgiving Day Falls City; Proctor Street Defends Cardinal Title


## Nov 19, 2026


Juddmonte’s 3-year-old filly Consequent will put her unbeaten record on the line against nine other fillies and mares in the 111th running of the $300,000 Falls City (Grade III), the centerpiece of a Thanksgiving stakes double at Churchill Downs.


Thanksgiving Day at Churchill Downs has been a Louisville tradition since 1969, serving around 7,500 turkey dinners with all the trimmings, making it the largest number anywhere in the region. The 1 1/8-mile Falls City goes as Race 11 at 4:14 p.m. (all times Eastern), and the 51st running of the $300,000 Cardinal presented by Resolute Racing (Listed) is scheduled as Race 9 at 3:16 p.m. First post is 11:30 a.m.


Trained by Hall of Famer Bob Baffert, Consequent has won all four of her starts, including the $200,000 Seneca Overnight Stakes (Listed) at Churchill Downs in mid-September. The daughter of Into Mischief made her first two starts in Southern California and won the $200,000 Starlet (GII) by a length as a 2-year-old. Flavien Prat will ride from post No. 3.


Among her rivals is Regaled, who won the $600,000 Delaware Handicap (GIII) on Oct. 3 by three lengths before finishing fifth in the Breeders’ Cup Distaff (GI), 5 ½ lengths behind winner Nitrogen. Trained by Whit Beckman for Ribble Farms, Hoolie Racing Stable and Kamp Racing, Regaled has won five of 25 starts and earned more than $1.3 million. Joe Ramos has the mount from post 8.


The complete lineup for the Falls City from the rail out (with jockey and trainer):


Miss Authentic (Francisco Arrieta, Anna Meah)
Take Charge Omaha (Mario Gutierrez, Matt Sims)
Consequent (Prat, Baffert)
Anna’s Promise (Luis Saez, Carlos David)
Yes It Tiz (Florent Geroux, Brad Cox)
So There She Was (Jose Ortiz, Brian Lynch)
Sugar Fish (Micah Husbands, Saffie Joseph Jr.)
Regaled (Ramos, Beckman)
Chasten (Tyler Gaffalione, Brad Cox)
The Falls City was created by Churchill Downs founder, Col. M. Lewis Clark, as one of four stakes events that were developed for the inaugural meet in 1875. The name, Falls City, is a reference to the Ohio River falls or rapids that drop some 30 feet just west of current downtown Louisville. The falls are the reason the city grew as riverboats were forced to unload their cargo on shore before reaching the falls. Clark’s original stakes schedule included the Kentucky Derby on Monday, the Kentucky Oaks on Wednesday, the Falls City Handicap on Thursday and the Clark on closing day, Saturday. The race has been run on Thanksgiving Day since 1978.


PROCTOR STREET RETURNS TO DEFEND TITLE IN $300,000 CARDINAL PRESENTED BY RESOLUTE RACING – Patricia Moseley’s Proctor Street returns to Churchill Downs on Thanksgiving to defend her title in the 51st running of the $300,000 Cardinal presented by Resolute Racing (Listed), one of two stakes on the holiday card.


The Cardinal will be contested at 1 1/8 miles on turf and goes as Race 9 at 3:16 p.m. The 12-race card also includes the $300,000 Falls City (GIII) as Race 11. First post is 11:30 a.m.


Trained by Brendan Walsh, Proctor Street won last year’s Cardinal by three-quarters of a length under Tyler Gaffalione. This year, the 5-year-old daughter of Street Sense won the $200,000 Canadian Stakes (GII) at Woodbine and finished second in the $275,000 Old Forester Mint Julep (GIII) at Churchill Downs in May. Gaffalione will be back aboard Thursday from post No. 10.


Walsh also entered Flying Dutchmen Breeding and Racing’s Hereforagoodtime, who recently won an allowance race at Keeneland. Walter Rodriguez has the mount from post 8.


Aside from Proctor Street, Walsh won the Cardinal in 2019 with Madaket Stables, Tim and Anna Cambron and Bradley Thoroughbreds’ Kallio.


Chief among her rivals in the race appears to be Steve Landers Racing’s Destino d’Oro, who won two Grade II stakes this winter for trainer Brad Cox. The 4-year-old daughter of Bolt d’Oro started her 2026 campaign by winning the $500,000 Pegasus World Cup Filly & Mare Turf Invitational at Gulfstream Park and the $225,000 Hillsborough Stakes at Tampa Bay Downs. Following more than six months on the sidelines, Destino d’Oro finished third in the $175,000 Forever Together Stakes on Sept. 20 at Belmont Park. Flavien Prat has the riding assignment in the Cardinal from post 7.


Cox previously won the Cardinal in 2016 with Richard and Bert Klein’s Cash Control.


The Cardinal field from the rail out (with jockey and trainer):


She’s Lookin Lucky (Florent Geroux, Matt Shirer)
Della Pace (GB) (Julien Leparoux, George Boughey)
Miwa (GB) (Jose Ortiz, Joe Sharp)
Caviar Breakfast (Manny Esquivel, Kenny McPeek)
Gallant Greta (Luis Saez, Mike Maker)
Vive Veuve (Brian Hernandez Jr., Joe Sharp)
Destino d’Oro (Prat, Cox)
Hereforagoodtime (Rodriguez, Walsh)
Totally Justified (Francisco Arrieta, Anna Meah)
Proctor Street (Gaffalione, Walsh)
Originally named the Kentucky Cardinal for the official state bird, the filly and mare contest for 3-year-olds and up was moved to the turf in 1987.
